core_obligations: Reduce to showing that the diagonal Delta : X -> X x_Y X is surjective (proof lines 6687-6689).
Assume the contrary, use closedness of the image (separatedness) to find a generic point eta of a component of X x_Y X outside it (proof lines 6690-6693).
Use flatness of pr_1 (a base change of f) and lifting of generalisations to see that xi = pr_1(eta) is a generic point of X (proof lines 6694-6699).
Apply assumptions (2) and (3) to see that the fibre over f(xi) has at most one point, so Delta(xi) = eta, a contradiction (proof lines 6700-6702).
proof_roadmap: Contradiction setup with a generic point eta (proof lines 6690-6693).
Flatness and lifting of generalisations (proof lines 6694-6699).
The fibre count and the contradiction (proof lines 6700-6702).
difficulty_reason: For a morphism f : X -> Y that is flat and separated, with trivial residue field extensions at the generic points of X and injective on those generic points, the lemma concludes that f is universally injective (statement lines 6675-6684). The proof reduces universal injectivity to surjectivity of the diagonal, argues by contradiction: if Delta misses a point then its image being closed lets one pick a generic point eta of a component of X x_Y X outside the image; the first projection is flat as a base change of f, so generalisations lift and the preimage xi of eta is a generic point of X; but the assumptions force the fibre (X x_Y X)_{f(xi)} to have at most one point, contradicting Delta(xi) = eta (proof lines 6687-6702). The level is H3: a genuine point-theoretic argument using flatness through the lifting of generalisations, with every step named.
